clue.text: Lay awake, finally, in awful trauma

definitions.note: lay as an adjective: not professional or expert

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of trauma, with that extra letter, are in a mess and must be rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word awake

explanation.surface: Someone lies sleepless at the end of the night, haunted by a dreadful shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb about lying awake, but it is the adjective meaning non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lay people are those without professional qualifications, which describes a non-professional.

clue.text: Just son supporting a female's romantic flings

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the just and son pieces sit below the others

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
just means fair

explanation.surface: A boy simply props up a woman during her romantic entanglements.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: affairs are love affairs, romantic relationships outside the usual ones.

clue.text: Changed a dressing, upsetting Edward

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the dressing word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a pad is a dressing for a wound
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A nurse changed a bandage, upsetting the patient Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something adapted has been altered or modified to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Go in chippy, wanting fish

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the fish word is removed

parts.note: chippy is British slang for a carpenter
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone enters a fish-and-chip shop but they're out of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippy' looks like a British chip shop, but here it is slang for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to enter a place is to go into it.

clue.text: Musical instruments — they create notes, perhaps

definitions.meaning: woodwind instruments played by blowing, common in schools
people or devices that write down notes or make records, such as minute-takers

explanation.surface: Instruments that produce musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple wooden pipe played in school bands, and also anyone who writes down notes of proceedings.

clue.text: Get ready before father starts to reproach everyone

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A child gets braced before Dad begins telling off the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make ready or to get things in order for an event.

clue.text: Factory temperature is below target

indicators.note: in a down clue, is below says the temperature piece comes after the target piece

parts.note: a plan is a goal or target

explanation.surface: A factory's heat output is falling short of its target.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a plant is an industrial works or factory.

clue.text: With no time, wildly post eleven Jiffy bags?

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of post eleven are rearranged
with no says a letter is taken out of the jumble

explanation.surface: In a hurry, someone frantically mails eleven padded packages.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T ('time', by 'With no') from POSTELEVEN and rearrange the rest ('wildly'). Jiffy is a British brand of padded mailing bag; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Jiffy bag is a padded postal wrapper for sending items through the mail.

clue.text: Almost everybody departing one country for another

indicators.note: departing means those letters leave the country word

parts.note: Australia is one country

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the everybody word is dropped

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone is leaving one nation for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts ALL to AL; 'departing' takes AL out of AUSTRALIA. The definition 'another' means another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the definition means a second nation, and this central European state is one.

clue.text: Some attend lessons — too many to be counted

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few pupils go to classes so numerous they can't be counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something infinite or limitless seems too numerous to count.

clue.text: Panic-stricken following tirade by one Conservative

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
a rant is a long angry tirade
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown into a panic after a Tory politician launches into an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone frantic is wildly agitated with fear or worry.

clue.text: Verse is to go after advertisement, editor suggested

indicators.note: to go after says the verse and is pieces follow the advertisement in the answer

explanation.surface: An editor proposes that a poem be printed after an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have advised something is to have recommended or put it forward.

clue.text: The printer's broken — not hard to understand

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of the words before it must be rearranged
not tells us one letter is left out of the jumble

parts.note: the word printer, with the 's read as is, a link
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An office complaint: the printer is broken, and it's not hard to see why.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', a link; rearrange THE PRINTER minus H (from 'hard', removed by 'not'), with 'broken' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to interpret something is to work out its meaning, to understand it.

clue.text: Big lake with flat-bottomed boat heading off

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: heading off says the front letter of the boat word is removed

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat used on canals and rivers

explanation.surface: A large lake with a barge setting off across it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the B of BARGE, leaving ARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: large and big both describe something of considerable size.

clue.text: Woefully speak about diamonds left

indicators.note: about means the speaking word goes around the next two pieces

parts.note: to say is to speak
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone talks mournfully about the diamonds they have left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done woefully is done sorrowfully, in an unhappy way.

clue.text: No rest with guy's new child

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the word guy, with the 's read as a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A man's newborn baby means no more sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a youngster is a young person, a child.

clue.text: Those from Rome, perhaps, could make Nero pause

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the next words can be rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: Romans might cause Emperor Nero to stop and think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Rome as one example of a city on the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Romans live in Italy, so they are among the people of the continent of Europe.

clue.text: Looks like doctor is in here less, unfortunately, having left hospital

indicators.note: is in says the doctor goes inside the rearranged letters
unfortunately signals that the letters are rearranged
having left says the hospital letter is removed

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor turns up at the ward less often, sadly, after quitting the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' takes H from HERELESS; 'unfortunately' rearranges ERELESS into RESELES; 'is in' puts MB inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that resembles another bears a likeness to it.

clue.text: Conceals most of meal with, I guess, bananas

indicators.note: most of says the last letter of the meal word is dropped

parts.note: a dish is a meal or course of food

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of I guess are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone hides most of their dinner, probably among some bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims DISH to DIS; 'bananas' rearranges IGUESS into GUISES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that disguises an object hides its true identity, concealing it.

clue.text: Hopelessness of the French couple

parts.note: des is French for of the (plural)
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: The misery of a French couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: despair is total loss of hope.

clue.text: Tug hands?

parts.note: hands are crew members, and a tug is a boat, so the crew of a tug are seafarers

explanation.surface: Reads like an instruction to pull someone's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tug' looks like a verb meaning pull, but it is a tugboat; 'hands' are its crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: hands are crew members, and those on a boat are seamen.

clue.text: Immoral acts involving grand gestures

indicators.note: involving means the sins word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: sins are immoral acts
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Wicked deeds accompanied by sweeping theatrical gestures.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: signs are gestures that convey a message, like a wave or a nod.

clue.text: Adult with note goes into class

indicators.note: goes into says those two letters sit inside the class word

parts.note: a group is a class or category

explanation.surface: A mature student hands a note in to class.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fully mature person is an adult.

clue.text: Spare shilling? Give an expression of hesitation

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin
to lend is to give for a time
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: Asked for a spare shilling, someone hesitates with an 'er'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like a request for money, but as an adjective it means thin. A shilling was a coin in Britain's old money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spare figure is lean or thin.

clue.text: Smart rock singer

definitions.meaning: to smart is to hurt with a sharp pain
the stage name of the lead singer of the band The Police

explanation.surface: A well-dressed and stylish rock vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp burning pain is a smart, and the Police frontman Gordon Sumner is known by this name.

clue.text: Order ministry to occupy key officer

indicators.note: to occupy says the order and ministry pieces sit inside the key word

parts.note: the core of something is its key or central part
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
MOD is the Ministry of Defence in Britain

explanation.surface: A command for the Defence Ministry to take over a key officer post.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a commodore is a naval officer ranking above captain.

clue.text: Found American leaving Greek island

indicators.note: leaving says the American letter goes out of the found word

parts.note: to found something is to create it

explanation.surface: Someone from the US sets up something and then leaves a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest of the Greek islands, in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Zero cost for lecture

parts.note: O looks like zero
a rate is a cost or charge

explanation.surface: A free talk, at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to orate is to deliver a formal speech, to lecture.

clue.text: Send in beer for John, maybe

indicators.note: in says the sending word goes inside the beer word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: An order to ship some beer over for a man called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is not a drinker but Saint John, one of the twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: John was one of the twelve disciples sent out by Jesus.

clue.text: Student deserved to be this?

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
something earned has been deserved

explanation.surface: A wondering question: did a student merit being called scholarly?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a student who has worked hard deserves to be well educated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone learned is scholarly and well read, what a diligent student aims to become.

clue.text: Doubt regarding Federer's first shot?

parts.note: re means regarding, as in business letters
Roger Federer is a tennis player, and a rally's first stroke in tennis is the serve

explanation.surface: A query about whether the tennis champion's opening stroke was good.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to accept something with reserve is to hold back doubt or reservation.

clue.text: Long, thin fish returned for a kipper

indicators.note: returned says the fish word is read backwards

parts.note: eels are long, thin fish
per means for a, as in ten pounds per head

explanation.surface: A slender fish sent back in exchange for a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper' looks like the smoked fish, but it means someone who kips, British slang for sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: to kip is to sleep, so a kipper is someone who sleeps.
